quote: Here was peace. She pulled in her horizon like a great fish-net. Pulled it from around the waist of the world and draped it over her shoulder. So much of life in its meshes! She called in her soul to come and see.
source: Zora Neale Hurston, Their Eyes Were Watching God, chapter 20, the closing sentences (J. B. Lippincott, 1937)

evidence.where: Internet Archive full text of the HarperCollins edition with the Edwidge Danticat foreword, which reprints the 1937 text; corroborated by Goodreads, LitCharts and eNotes
evidence.edition: HarperCollins (Perennial Modern Classics), foreword by Edwidge Danticat; text of J. B. Lippincott, 1937
evidence.locator: last five sentences of chapter 20, the end of the novel

reason: The five sentences close the novel word for word in the reprint text, fish-net hyphenated. The preceding sentences about the gun and the body are excluded, so the excerpt is publishable. Hurston stands at one of three (May).
